### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-bundle-members.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-bundle-members.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b3afb04865b97eb921b93bd4f38d0ceab19a6e37` — the merge of head `ce8d6e76ff3500b36b3cfc63d243027817c0540f` into base `e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b3afb04865b97eb921b93bd4f38d0ceab19a6e37 && git checkout b3afb04865b97eb921b93bd4f38d0ceab19a6e37
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42 ce8d6e76ff3500b36b3cfc63d243027817c0540f && git checkout -B drift-repro e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42 && git merge --no-ff ce8d6e76ff3500b36b3cfc63d243027817c0540f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L2 round on head 90b5cdeb4f: S1 and S2 sent back, seat ruling on S1 · 2026-11-17T22:56Z

The seat's at-tier reviewer sub-agent read this head and found no must-fix and two should-fix. Its record is NOT posted as the record of this head: its transcript holds a synthetic usage-limit turn, which `verify-review-tier.mjs` refuses. The fresh at-tier record is rendered on the fixed head.

**S1 (should-fix): the holder's first member still reaches both reads at an exact address.** `readMetaItem` and `getMetaItemLayered` end an exact address in `exactQualifierItem(…, member)` (`protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`). When the item in hand is another package's, it is replaced by `registry.getPackageScopedItem(type, name, holder, member)` with the raw selector. Naming no member, that answers canonical-first, else the holder's first member. So, read from the tree and not run, at an exact address the read naming no member still differs from `?member=en-US` whenever another package holds the canonical member. The base-address mirror and the re-addressed read move with it. `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts` asserts the old answer on purpose.

**Seat ruling on S1: exit (a).**
Ruling-ref: the governing text is the selector sentence in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (~399-403): "Absent, the canonical member … which is what a bare-name read answers; naming the canonical value is the same request … a well-formed member with nothing stored or shipped answers as that door answers an absent item."
SKILL.md: spec and code disagree ⇒ align the code. This is the card's own defect at a third site, not a new product decision; the pin that asserts the old answer asserts the departure from that sentence, so it flips.
- Hold the replacement to the addressed member in both reads.
- Flip that pin's last leg.
- Pin the base-address mirror (naming no member equals naming `en-US`, at the address and through the re-address).
- Name the exact address in the ledger entry.

**S2 (should-fix): the ledger entry names less than the diff moves.** `18.bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent.ts` quantifies over a name "that no layer ships or stores in its canonical member", but the diff also moves the read naming no member where a dependent stores the canonical member over a base that ships only another one. The sibling `18.shipped-base-dependent-canonical-row-not-published.ts` (unshipped, same step) ends "The plain read, ?member=CANONICAL and the execution read do not move", which is now false. Fix: name the arrangement in the new entry, and correct the sibling's last sentence.

**Pending changeset correction.** `.changeset/34441-shipped-base-canonical-member-one-answer.md` (pending on `main`) states two answers this PR reverses (`/layers` naming no member "TO A's `fr-FR` (200)", and the plain read under "Not moved"). It is amended in this PR as a DELIBERATE CORRECTION of another PR's pending note (never `skip-changeset`). The seat's ACCEPT confirms each changed sentence.

Nits sent along: N1 (the layered comment on the removed lookup), N2 (one preserved-half leg per name at the doors), N3 (the `/published` mixed-holder guard: residue card if needed).
